newsitem.title: ITALY: BankItaly's Fazio sees CPI outlook improving.
newsitem.headline: BankItaly's Fazio sees CPI outlook improving.

text.p: Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said expectations for inflation were improving but warned there was a possible inflation risk from labour costs, output prices and insufficient action to control the budget deficit.
"Forecasts made in December indicate that for the first half of this year inflation will be between 2.5 and three percent," Fazio told a foreign exchange trading convention.
Preliminary January inflation data last week showed consumer prices growing at 0.2 percent month on month and 2.6 percent year on year compared with final December data of 0.1 percent and 2.6.
Fazio said from May to December 1996 the average of month on month inflation analysed over a year was around two percent.
"According to preliminary data in January the growth of prices was less than two percent," he said.
The Bank of Italy cut its key discount and fixed term advances or Lombard rates 75 basis points last Tuesday, bringing them down to 6.75 and 8.25 percent respectively.
Fazio said: "The reduction in official rates, which follows those made in 1996, was made possible by the actual and expected improvement in inflation."
However Fazio said he saw possible inflation risks from labour costs and other potential pressures on prices.

"Starting and maintaining the virtuous circle could be interrupted by the reappearance of inflationary pressures, which could come from labour costs, companies' pricing policy... from insufficient correction or excessive expansion of the deficit," he said.

"Rebalancing of the public deficit must be carried out limiting growth in spending. On the revenue side it is necessary to reduce evasion. (More taxes) would have negative effects on internal demand and on prices," he said.
"In order to encourage confidence...the corrections to the public accounts must have a structural character," he added.
